title: MapleBridge embeddings + reranker hosted API overview
summary: Introductory hosted API demo focused on embeddings + reranking for search relevance. Covered model choices, quantization/cost tradeoffs, batching and KV cache, VPC/data residency concerns, and a short Console walkthrough for rerank configs. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated with a 3-month pilot target; next steps include sharing benchmarks, security docs, and a pilot proposal.
transcript:
[00:00] Evan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Evan from Redwood, my teammate Maya is here on the deep tech side. quick roll call?
[00:06] Jordan (MapleBridge): Jordan here, Casey and Asha are with me. thanks for doing this.
[00:10] Maya (Redwood SE): Hey all — I'll kick off with a short agenda, then we'll jump into the Console and API. we want to show embeddings flow + reranker pipeline and how you'd set up a pilot.
[00:22] Casey (MapleBridge): Sounds good. our main pain is search relevance for product docs; current vector store is slow and not consistent across regions. cost is a factor, too.
[00:33] Evan: Great, that's helpful. what's your current stack for embeddings and vectors — self-hosted FAISS? pinecone?
[00:39] Jordan: We're on an in-house vector store built over FAISS with a small microservice wrapping it. embeddings are a mix — some open models, some homegrown.
[00:46] Asha: Timeline wise we want a pilot in the next 6 weeks and a decision by end of Q3.
[00:52] Maya: Perfect. quick qualifier on requirements — data residency/regulatory needs? do you need VPC or air-gapped?
[00:58] Jordan: We need EU data residency for EU customers. For now hosted is fine if there's a VPC option and encryption at rest with customer-managed keys.
[01:08] Maya: Totally — Redwood Hosted supports customer VPC peering and integration with KMS/HSM for keys. SOC 2 is supported; we can share the report.
[01:19] Casey: When you say "KV cache" in the docs, is that the same as prefix caching? we've seen references to "K V cash" in a few places in our notes.
[01:27] Maya: (laughs) yes, it's the key-value cache, prefix caching of decoder states — it's good for conversation or repeated prefixes. reduces tokens and latency for similar context.
[01:36] Evan: Ok jumping into the Console — I'll share my screen, you'll see the model catalog first. for embeddings we recommend one of the mid-sized open models for cost-effective nearest neighbor recall, then a small reranker model for final scoring.
[01:49] Jordan: do you support quantized variants? we need to trim costs but keep decent quality.
[01:54] Maya: Yes, we have quantized model profiles and the runtime will auto-select GPU kernels and quantization paths based on your SLA and sequence length. in the Console you can pick a quant profile per model.
[02:06] Casey: what's the expected latency difference between hosted and dedicated? ballpark numbers per 512-token query?
[02:13] Maya: For hosted embeddings it's typically 30-70 ms per request for small models, reranker steps add 50-150 ms depending on sequence length and batch. dedicated reduces variance and can push medians lower if you reserve capacity.
[02:26] Jordan: And batching — do we control batch sizes? we worry about p95 blips when batching groups accumulate.
[02:31] Maya: There's intelligent batching that is workload-aware; you can also set max-latency budgets and disable batching for low-latency routes. Redwood Optimize will suggest batching thresholds to hit cost targets without breaching SLOs.
[02:45] Asha: can you show an end-to-end run — embedding a query, retrieving neighbors, running the reranker?
[02:50] Evan: Yup — I'll switch to the API tab. here's a simple flow: call /embeddings to get vectors, then do a knn in your vector DB, then send candidate docs to /rerank with structured payload.
[03:03] [03:03] Evan: (typing) the rerank endpoint accepts a list of candidate ids + contexts, you can pass metadata, and get back a score and an optional explanation field. the response can be streamed.
[03:15] Casey: that explanation field — is it deterministic, or model-dependent? we've seen flaky explanations in other systems.
[03:21] Maya: It's model-dependent and can vary. we expose a deterministic scoring mode if you supply the same model+prompt+seed, but free-text explanations can vary. we recommend using the score for programmatic decisions.
[03:33] Jordan: With the EU residency constraint — will data transit through US region during inference?
[03:38] Evan: You can pin region and we support EU-hosted inference and routing. for strict needs, Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) can keep inference within your network.
[03:48] Casey: Awesome. what's the per-token pricing on the reranker path compared to standard generation?
[03:53] Evan: Pricing varies by model; reranker uses shorter sequences typically so unit cost is lower than generative LLM calls, but you multiply by number of candidates — so the optimization is in candidate count and batching. Redwood Optimize can simulate cost/latency for different candidate counts.
[04:10] Asha: do you have a quick demo of Optimize suggestions?
[04:13] Maya: Sure — here's the Optimize tab, it shows token-level cost breakdown, candidate count impact, and a recommended quant profile. you can run a simulated workload with your trace or upload samples.
[04:26] Jordan: You mentioned automatic fallback — if capacity in EU is constrained, how does Redwood handle fallbacks without violating residency?
[04:33] Maya: By policy. for EU-restricted customers we won't route outside the region; fallback could be to a lower-capacity model in-region, or enroll auto-provisioned dedicated nodes. we'll surface options in Console.
[04:46] Casey: any gotchas with vector stores — we use FAISS sharded across clusters. can Redwood handle batched fetches or do you expect us to pull candidates individually?
[04:55] Evan: We recommend pulling top-K per query from your store (batched RPCs are fine) and passing the candidates in a single /rerank call. that keeps network hops low. some customers integrate Redis or Milvus; we've seen good results with batched candidates.
[05:08] Jordan: Security docs? we need SOC2 + encryption details and a data flow diagram.
[05:12] Evan: We'll share the SOC 2 report, network diagram, and KMS integration guide after the call.
[05:18] Asha: ok, next I'm curious about model drift — how do you monitor quality over time?
[05:23] Maya: Redwood Optimize supports quality monitors tied to prompt sets and evals. you can set regression alerts and roll back model versions automatically. also can tie to sampling of live queries.
[05:35] Casey: about pilot engineering — what's the minimum footprint to start? do we need dedicated capacity?
[05:40] Evan: For a pilot we usually start hosted with a staged traffic plan: low traffic and telemetry to measure p95 and cost. dedicated only if you need strict throughput or isolation.
[05:51] Jordan: What about SDKs — do we have a python client for quick integration?
[05:55] Maya: Yes, there's Python and Node SDKs, and example notebooks for embeddings+rerkank flows.
[06:01] Evan: (interruption) small note — sometimes the transcript will show wrong punctuation; sorry if any terms sound odd.
[06:06] Jordan: yeah earlier we saw "K V cash" in the doc, that made us laugh.
[06:10] Maya: (laugh) noted.
[06:12] Evan: Alright, quick perf numbers — here's a benchmark sheet link: (shared) — it's a host of sample workloads.
[06:20] Casey: can you run a quick demo with one of our sample queries? we've pre-shared a CSV in the deal folder.
[06:26] Evan: We didn't load that live but we can do a mocked query to show latencies. running an embeddings call now...
[06:34] [06:34] Evan: Embedding request returned 42ms, passing top-10 candidates to reranker, rerank returned 120ms total.
[06:45] Jordan: that's promising. If we scale to 200 qps, what's the guidance?
[06:50] Maya: For 200 qps steady you may want a mix: hosted with reserved capacity or Dedicated. Redwood can estimate node counts based on model and seq length. we'll include capacity recommendations in the follow-up.
[07:04] Asha: any contract minimums for Dedicated?
[07:08] Evan: Dedicated is typically monthly commitments; we'll propose pilot pricing for hosted then a committed offer if you want reserved nodes.
[07:20] Casey: are there rate limits per-token or per-route we should anticipate?
[07:24] Maya: There are default rate limits on hosted accounts but they can be increased per-customer. for pilots we usually lift to match the test.
[07:32] Jordan: One more technical: do you preserve user PII in logs? we need to know retention and redaction options.
[07:38] Evan: Logs retention is configurable; we offer automatic PII redaction and can set short retention windows for sensitive workloads.
[07:46] Asha: ok this is helpful. let's recap next steps.
[07:50] Evan: Recap: we'll share SOC2 + network diagram, a benchmark spreadsheet with modeled costs at 200 qps, and a pilot proposal. Maya will run a short technical onboarding with Casey next week.
[08:02] Maya: I'll follow up with a hands-on sandbox link and the example notebook.
[08:08] Jordan: Great. any blockers from our side? Casey will validate sample queries and we'll review the security docs.
[08:16] Evan: Perfect. thanks everyone, we'll send follow-ups and get that pilot scoped.
[08:20] Asha: Thanks all.
[08:22] [END]
